text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000114 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but the few charts returned all support the billed level, so the evidence points both ways.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by panel mix: the 99215 share runs at roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every chronic-condition band, and billing is compressed toward 99214/99215 with almost no low-level visits, which fits a uniform coding habit rather than a sicker panel alone. Against that, most 99215s fall on multi-morbid patients, all 7 documented 99215s were supported at high MDM (e.g., C0051562, C0051924), and there is no sign of inflated data-review notes on claims lacking lab or test lines. The documentation is too thin to settle the question, because records cover under 1% of claims and only 7 are 99215s. A reviewer should first pull a larger targeted chart sample, starting with sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0051802 (rash, no chronic conditions), C0053120 (back pain, no chronic conditions) and the single-condition follow-up (Z09) visits like C0050947 and C0052973. The reviewer should also check whether the high-band 99215s show visit-specific MDM rather than templated notes."}
